stories.title: Wire learning feedback loop — persist trade outcomes to SQLite
stories.goal: After every trade closes in tracker.py, call process_trade_outcome() from learning/feedback.py and persist the structured result to a new trade_outcomes SQLite table. This is JARVIS's long-term memory store — every closed trade creates a permanent record with symbol, action, pnl, outcome, regime context, and lesson_text.
acceptanceCriteria: trade_outcomes SQLite table created via migration: trade_id TEXT PK, symbol TEXT, action TEXT, pnl REAL, outcome TEXT (win/loss/scratch), entry_time TEXT, exit_time TEXT, duration_seconds INTEGER, lesson_type TEXT, lesson_text TEXT, created_at TEXT
tracker.py close_trade() calls process_trade_outcome() from learning/feedback.py after successful SQLite write — fire-and-forget (asyncio.create_task or threading.Thread)
feedback result is persisted to trade_outcomes table — all fields populated
process_trade_outcome() failure is caught and logged — never blocks trade close
GET /learning/outcomes endpoint added — returns trade_outcomes from SQLite (for verification)
After closing a paper trade via POST /portfolio/paper/close/{trade_id}, GET /learning/outcomes returns 1+ rows
cd engine && .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest tests/ -v passes with 0 failures
stories.notes: learning/feedback.py already has process_trade_outcome() fully implemented. It generates TradeOutcomeFeedback with lesson_type and lesson_text. The ONLY missing pieces are: (1) call it from close_trade(), (2) create the trade_outcomes SQLite table, (3) persist the result. Do NOT modify feedback.py logic — just wire the call and the persistence.

stories.title: Inject learning context into pipeline — JARVIS remembers before it decides
stories.goal: Before Stage 1 of the pipeline runs, query trade_outcomes for the last 20 closed trades on the symbol being analyzed. Format a Historical Trading Context summary. Inject it into the TechnicalAnalyst and TraderAgent system prompts so every decision is informed by what actually happened last time JARVIS traded this symbol.
acceptanceCriteria: learning/recommendations.py: add get_trade_history_context(symbol, limit=20) function that queries trade_outcomes SQLite table and returns a formatted string like: 'JARVIS TRADE HISTORY — MCL (last 5 trades): 3 wins / 2 losses (60% WR). Avg winner: +$95 | Avg loser: -$45. Last trade: LONG closed +$100 (2h 14m). Most recent loss: SHORT -$45.'
pipeline.py: before Stage 1 (TechnicalAnalyst call), call get_trade_history_context(symbol) and store result in pipeline_context dict
TechnicalAnalyst agent system prompt includes the history context block when it contains data (when trade_outcomes has rows for this symbol)
When trade_outcomes is empty (no history yet), context block is omitted gracefully — no error, no empty placeholder injected
Pipeline run result includes learning_context_injected: true/false field
cd engine && .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest tests/ -v passes with 0 failures
Manual pipeline trigger via POST /scanner/trigger shows learning_context_injected in pipeline_runs or logs
stories.notes: learning/recommendations.py already has get_recommendations() scaffolded. Create get_trade_history_context() as a NEW simpler function that reads directly from trade_outcomes SQLite table (not the patterns layer which needs a db_manager). The query: SELECT symbol, action, pnl, outcome, lesson_text FROM trade_outcomes WHERE symbol=? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20. Format as a concise block. Keep under 300 tokens — must not bloat the LLM prompt.

stories.title: Audit LLM agent data feeds — confirm real data reaches every agent
stories.goal: Add structured input logging to every Stage 1 agent (TechnicalAnalyst, NewsAnalyst, SocialAnalyst, FundamentalistAgent). After triggering a manual scan, read the logs to confirm what data each agent actually received. Fix any agent receiving empty/fallback data by identifying and patching its data source.
acceptanceCriteria: Each Stage 1 agent logs at INFO level at the START of its analyze() method: '[AGENT_INPUT] {AgentName} received: {summary of actual data}' — e.g. '[AGENT_INPUT] NewsAnalyst received: 3 headlines for MCL, source=polygon'
After POST /scanner/trigger, engine logs show 4 [AGENT_INPUT] lines — one per agent — within 30 seconds
For each agent, determine: is it receiving real data (Polygon/Finnhub/IB) or falling back to empty/None?
If NewsAnalyst is receiving 0 headlines: diagnose why (Polygon key issue? wrong endpoint? rate limit?) and fix
If SocialAnalyst is receiving None sentiment: diagnose and fix or implement graceful fallback text that says 'No social data available — neutral assumption'

If FundamentalistAgent is receiving empty fundamentals: diagnose and implement fallback (futures have no P/E — the fallback should be macro context: VIX level, yield curve data if available, or explicit 'no fundamental data for futures — using macro regime only')
Write docs/reports/sprint22_agent_audit.md — one section per agent with: what it received, what source, pass/fail, fix applied if any
cd engine && .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest tests/ -v passes with 0 failures
stories.notes: The most likely finding: NewsAnalyst gets 0 headlines (Polygon news key may be on free tier with no news access), SocialAnalyst gets None (social sentiment API may not be configured), FundamentalistAgent gets empty dict (futures have no traditional fundamentals — the agent needs a macro fallback). Do not fake data — implement honest fallbacks that tell the LLM 'I have no data in this category, assume neutral.' This is better than hallucinated data.

stories.title: WhatsApp reply approval — one-word approve from phone
stories.goal: Wire OpenClaw inbound message listener so Matt can reply 'yes', 'no', or 'hold' to a WhatsApp approval alert and JARVIS instantly approves/rejects the pending trade. This transforms JARVIS from a notification system into a two-way collaborator.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /openclaw/webhook endpoint added to engine — receives incoming OpenClaw webhook payload
Endpoint parses message body: 'yes' or 'approve' → approve the most recent pending_trade_approvals row; 'no' or 'reject' → reject it; 'hold' or 'skip' → leave it pending
After approving: POST /portfolio/paper/trade is called internally to open the paper position
After rejecting: pending_trade_approvals row status updated to 'rejected' with rejected_at timestamp
Confirmation WhatsApp sent back via OpenClaw: 'JARVIS: Trade approved — MCL LONG @ $72.50 opened' or 'JARVIS: Trade rejected'
Endpoint is idempotent — if no pending approvals exist, replies 'JARVIS: No pending trades to approve'
Endpoint is protected (verify sender is the registered OpenClaw phone number from config)
Write docs/runbooks/whatsapp_approval.md — how to configure OpenClaw webhook URL, test procedure
cd engine && .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest tests/ -v passes with 0 failures
stories.notes: OpenClaw runs on port 8009. Check OpenClaw documentation or endpoint list for how to register a webhook for incoming messages. The webhook registration may require a POST to http://localhost:8009/api/oc/webhook/register or similar. The JARVIS engine webhook URL to register would be http://localhost:8010/openclaw/webhook. Check engine/notifications/openclaw_notifier.py for any existing webhook registration code or OpenClaw API patterns already established.
